title: Worker-First Harness Prompt Doctrine
subtitle: Make the living-doc worker the main actuator of objective progress
scope: Prompt doctrine repair for living-doc harness inference units.
sourceCoverage: Session-derived objective from prompt overview review; grounded in harness prompt builders and inference-unit registry.
objective: Repair the living-doc harness inference-unit prompt doctrine so the worker is clearly the primary actuator of objective progress and every supporting unit routes back toward real work unless a concrete gate, missing decision, or proven structural repair need blocks it. The prompt set must define the living doc as the active working surface for the objective: the place where source-system state, evidence, unresolved terms, acceptance criteria, and current truth are kept aligned. The revised prompts must preserve controller-owned routing and closure safety while making avoidance visible and invalid: units may inspect, gate, repair, or review only in service of returning the lifecycle to meaningful source-system or living-doc progress.
successCondition: The objective is met only when the generated prompt surface and contract tests prove a worker-first hierarchy: the worker prompt requires concrete objective progress when knowable; every supporting unit states how it serves return-to-work, narrow repair, side-effect gating, review, or terminal guard duty; living-doc purpose is present in the prompt stack; avoidance-shaped outputs are explicitly invalid; and the full harness contract suite remains green.

objectiveFacets.label: Worker as primary actuator
objectiveFacets.description: The worker prompt must make concrete source-system or living-doc progress the default action.

objectiveFacets.label: Living doc purpose
objectiveFacets.description: The prompt stack must describe the living doc as the working surface for objective state, evidence, source alignment, unresolved decisions, and current truth.

objectiveFacets.label: Supporting units serve return-to-work
objectiveFacets.description: Reviewer, continuation, balance scan, repair, commit, PR, and closure units must be subordinate to real work or safe closure.

objectiveFacets.label: Avoidance invalid
objectiveFacets.description: Scans, summaries, blocker labels, report polish, or route churn cannot count as progress unless they advance, repair, gate, or expose a real missing condition.

objectiveFacets.label: Safety preserved
objectiveFacets.description: Controller-owned routing, artifact-ref continuity, closure-review authority, and side-effect gates remain intact.

invariants.statement: When the next objective move is knowable and allowed, the worker prompt must prefer doing real source-system or living-doc work over declaring a blocker or routing away.
The living doc must be described as the active objective state surface, not merely a JSON file or after-the-fact report.
Supporting units may inspect, gate, review, or repair, but they must not become broad substitutes for worker implementation.
Worker-first prompting must not weaken controller-owned routing, closure review, artifact-ref handoff, or side-effect gates.

sections.title: Plain-Language Analogy
sections.summary: A household analogy for the worker-first prompt doctrine.

data.title: Parent telling kids how to make money
data.objectiveExplanation: The worker is the kid who has to go out and earn; if the next honest thing to do is knowable, do it instead of coming back with plans, excuses, or another request for someone else to decide. The living doc is the family notebook: it records the job, the promise, what was tried, what worked, what is still missing, and the receipts.
data.currentState: The other units are helpers in the house: they can check the work, fix a specific mistake, make sure rules were followed, or decide whether the job is really done. They are not there so the worker can avoid earning; when someone says money was made, the system expects work, a receipt, an updated notebook, and a clear account of what remains unpaid.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
sections.summary: Closure gates for repairing the harness prompt doctrine.

data.title: Worker prompt makes worker the default progress engine
data.objectiveTerm: worker is clearly the primary actuator of objective progress
data.criterion: The worker prompt explicitly says it should make the next concrete source-system or living-doc move when knowable, and only return a blocker after naming exhausted local moves and the exact missing condition.
data.proofRequired: Generated worker prompt text and a contract test that checks for worker-first progress language.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if the worker prompt can omit the default-to-real-work instruction.
data.proofObserved: scripts/living-doc-harness-runner.mjs worker prompt now says the worker is the primary actuator, should do the next knowable source-system or living-doc move, and should only return a blocker after concrete local moves.

data.title: Living doc purpose is defined in the prompt stack
data.objectiveTerm: living doc as the active working surface
data.criterion: Relevant prompts describe the living doc as the working surface for objective state, evidence, source-system alignment, unresolved decisions, acceptance criteria, and current truth.
data.proofRequired: Prompt overview and prompt contract tests show the living-doc-purpose language across the prompt stack.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if prompts only describe the living doc as background JSON, a report, or proof artifact.
data.proofObserved: Shared runner and reviewer/closure prompts define the living doc as the active working surface for objective state, source-system state, evidence, unresolved decisions, acceptance criteria, and current truth.

data.title: Supporting units are subordinate to worker progress
data.objectiveTerm: every supporting unit routes back toward real work
data.criterion: Reviewer, balance-scan, repair-skill, continuation, commit-intent, PR-review, and closure-review prompts each state how their role serves return-to-work, narrow repair, gate satisfaction, review, or safe terminal closure.
data.proofRequired: Generated prompt overview shows role-subordination language for each supporting unit.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if a supporting prompt can read as an independent progress engine without routing back to worker or a concrete gate.
data.proofObserved: Supporting prompt builders now state their return-to-work, narrow repair, gate, review, continuation, or terminal-guard role.

data.title: Avoidance is explicitly invalid
data.criterion: Prompts reject progress-shaped artifacts such as scans, summaries, blocker labels, report polish, or route churn when they do not advance the objective, repair the living doc, satisfy a gate, or expose a real missing condition.
data.proofRequired: Prompt wording plus tests that assert avoidance-invalid language exists in worker, reviewer, and continuation prompts.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if route churn or blocker labeling can be framed as sufficient progress without objective movement or a real missing condition.
data.proofObserved: Worker, reviewer, and repair-skill prompts reject scans, summaries, blocker labels, report polish, and route churn when they do not move the objective or expose a real missing condition.

data.title: Reviewer checks progress, not just closure
data.objectiveTerm: reviewer routes back toward real work
data.criterion: Reviewer prompt asks whether the worker materially advanced source state, living-doc truth, evidence, or unresolved acceptance criteria before deciding the next state.
data.proofRequired: Generated reviewer prompt text and contract test coverage.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if reviewer prompt only checks closure gates and raw log inspection without checking material progress.
data.proofObserved: Reviewer prompt now asks whether the worker materially advanced source state, living-doc truth, evidence, or resolved acceptance criteria.

data.title: Continuation routes toward productive work
data.criterion: Continuation prompt prefers returning to worker unless evidence shows a specific repair skill, side-effect gate, PR-review gate, or user decision is required.
data.proofRequired: Generated continuation prompt text and prompt contract test coverage.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if continuation can default to more continuation without a changed reason, concrete repair, gate, or missing decision.
data.proofObserved: Continuation prompt now prefers returning to worker unless evidence names repair, commit-intent, PR-review, or user-decision requirements.

data.title: Balance-scan is not a default detour
data.criterion: Balance-scan prompt is limited to structural living-doc imbalance and cannot substitute for ordinary worker progress.
data.proofRequired: Generated balance-scan prompt text and role-boundary assertion.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if balance-scan prompt permits broad implementation work or generic avoidance.
data.proofObserved: Balance-scan prompt now says it is only for structural living-doc imbalance and cannot substitute for ordinary worker progress.

data.title: Repair-skill stays narrow
data.criterion: Repair-skill prompt repairs a named doc/objective/evidence defect and then returns control toward worker or the required gate; it cannot become a general worker replacement.
data.proofRequired: Generated repair-skill prompt text and role-boundary assertion.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if repair-skill prompt can take over broad objective implementation.
data.proofObserved: Repair-skill prompt now says it repairs only the named doc/objective/evidence defect and must not become a general worker replacement.

data.title: Gate units do not become progress engines
data.criterion: Commit-intent and PR-review prompts define themselves as side-effect or evidence gates, not units that solve the objective.
data.proofRequired: Generated commit-intent and PR-review prompt text.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if gate prompts can request broad implementation work instead of gate evidence.
data.proofObserved: Commit-intent and PR-review prompts now explicitly call themselves evidence gates, not objective-progress engines.

data.title: Closure-review remains terminal guard only
data.criterion: Closure-review prompt cannot request broad new work except by returning a concrete denial reason that routes to continuation or worker.
data.proofRequired: Generated closure-review prompt text and contract test coverage.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails if closure-review can act as worker, repair unit, or source editor.
data.proofObserved: Closure-review prompt now states terminal guard duty only and requires a concrete denial reason when closure is blocked.

data.title: Prompt overview shows revised hierarchy
data.criterion: The static prompt overview page is regenerated and shows the revised worker-first hierarchy and living-doc doctrine for every unit.
data.acceptanceTest: The page visibly distinguishes worker-as-actuator from supporting review, repair, gate, continuation, and closure units.
data.proofObserved: docs/living-doc-harness-inference-unit-prompts-overview.html was updated with the worker-first hierarchy and revised unit skeletons.

data.title: Prompt behavior has contract coverage
data.criterion: Tests or fixtures assert worker-first and living-doc-purpose wording exists in generated prompts and that continuation/reviewer prompts cannot omit return-to-work language.
data.proofRequired: Contract test file or expanded existing harness prompt tests.
data.acceptanceTest: The test fails on omission of worker-first, living-doc-purpose, or return-to-work language.
data.proofObserved: tests/contract/living-doc-harness-prompt-doctrine.spec.mjs generates worker, continuation, and reviewer prompts, checks prompt-builder doctrine text, and is included in npm run test:contract.

data.title: Existing safety invariants remain intact
data.objectiveTerm: preserve controller-owned routing and closure safety
data.criterion: `npm run test:contract` still passes, including controller-owned routing, artifact-ref, closure-review, side-effect gate, and monkey tests.
data.proofRequired: Local test output from `npm run test:contract`.
data.acceptanceTest: The objective cannot close if prompt changes break the contract suite.
data.proofObserved: npm run test:contract passed after the prompt doctrine changes.
